title: Dividing Complex Numbers
short: Multiply by the conjugate to clear i from the denominator.

blocks.html: Dividing by a complex number looks awkward: what is $\frac{1}{2 + i}$ in the form $a + bi$? The tool is something you saw in Adding and Multiplying Complex Numbers: a number times its conjugate is real. It is the same trick as rationalizing a denominator with a square root.

To divide, multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator (change the sign of its $i$ part). The denominator becomes the real number $c^2 + d^2$, and then you split the fraction into $a + bi$.

Multiplying by $\frac{c - di}{c - di}$ is multiplying by 1, so the value does not change. The point is the denominator: $(c + di)(c - di) = c^2 - d^2i^2$ $= c^2 + d^2$, a positive real number. Once the denominator is real, dividing is just dividing each part by an ordinary number.

blocks.name: complexplane
blocks.cap: Division undoes multiplication. Drag $z$ and $w$ and compare the quotient with $z$; then switch to "mul" to see how multiplying by $w$ undoes it.

blocks.title: A whole-number answer
steps: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate $1 + i$.

blocks.title: Fractions in the answer
steps: Multiply by $\frac{2 - i}{2 - i}$: bottom $4 + 1 = 5$, top $2 - i$.

blocks.title: Dividing by a pure imaginary number
steps: The conjugate of $2i$ is $-2i$, but multiplying by $i$ also works: $$\frac{(6 - 4i)i}{2i \cdot i} = \frac{6i - 4i^2}{2i^2} = \frac{4 + 6i}{-2}.$$

blocks.html: Multiplying only the denominator by the conjugate. That changes the value of the fraction. You must multiply the top and the bottom by the same thing, so you are multiplying by 1. Check any answer by multiplying it back by the denominator.
